C: A1 [ C ] the regular work that a person does to earn money
A2 [ C ] a particular piece of work

S: B2 [ S ] something that is your responsibility
› [ S ] informal a problem or an activity that is difficult

C: › [ C ] informal an example of a particular type
› [ C ] slang a crime in which money or goods are stolen, or an action or activity that is dishonest or unpleasant

example: a temporary/permanent job
臨時的／固定的工作
When she left college, she got a job as an editor in a publishing company.
大學畢業後她在一家出版社當編輯。
It's very difficult trying to bring up two children while doing a full-time job.
一邊撫育兩個孩子一邊做全職工作很困難。
He's never managed to hold down (= keep) a steady (= permanent) job.
他從來沒能保住一份穩定的工作。
She's applied for a job with an insurance company.
她已向一家保險公司應徵。
Are you going to give up your job when you have your baby?
你有了小孩後會放棄工作嗎？
After a disastrous first month in office, many people are beginning to wonder if the new president is up to (= able to do) the job.
由於新總統任職的第一個月表現很糟，許多人開始懷疑他是否勝任。
Hundreds of workers could lose their jobs.
數百名工人可能會失業。
How long have you been out of a job?
你沒有工作已有多久了？
Synonym
unemployed
The builders are aiming to get the job done by the end of the month.
施工人員打算在月底前將工作完成。
He spent the afternoon doing jobs around the house.
他整個下午都在家裡做雜務。
informal Will you be able to carry all the shopping back home on your bike, or will it have to be a car job (= will you need the car)?
你能把買來的東西都用腳踏車載回家嗎，還是用汽車才行？
[ + to infinitive ] She believed her job as a politician was to represent the views of her party and the people who voted for her.
她認為自己身為政治家的職責就是要做自己政黨和選民的代言人。
I know it's not my job to tell you how to run your life, but I do think you've made a mistake.
我知道不該由我來告訴你如何生活，但我的確認為你犯了錯。

[ + -ing verb ] It was a real job getting the wheel off the bike.
把腳踏車的輪子拆下來可真費力。
We were only given an hour for the exam, and I had a job finishing it.
我們的考試限時一小時，我好不容易才做完。
It's an original, not one of those imitation jobs.
這是原作，不是仿製品。
He was put in prison for five years for doing a bank job.
他因搶劫銀行被判入獄五年。
US He really did a job on her, telling her that he would always love her and then moving to Fiji with someone else.
他的確耍了她，告訴她自己會永遠愛她，後來卻和別人一起跑到斐濟去了。

NONE: › a temporary show of dissatisfaction by a group of workers, often by doing their work more slowly, in order to make managers pay attention to their demands
職工抗議行動
› a government office where unemployed people can go for advice and information about jobs that are available
就業服務中心
› the process of providing new jobs, especially for people who are unemployed
創造就業（尤指為失業者提供新工作）

example: the government's job creation strategy
政府的創造就業策略

NONE: › a list of the responsibilities that you have and the duties that you are expected to perform in your work
職務描述
› something you say when someone has achieved something, especially when it seems easier or quicker than you expected
做得好（某人做成某事時所說的話，尤其是比想像的更容易、更快時）

example: I just changed the fuse in the plug and the lamp worked, job done.
我只是簡單地換了插頭的保險絲，燈就亮了，輕鬆搞定。

NONE: › the process of comparing a job with other jobs in an organization and deciding how much the person who is doing the job should be paid
工作評估；職位評定
› a collection of various objects that are bought or sold as a group, usually at a low price
（以較低價格買賣的）一批雜貨

example: I bought a job lot of second-hand children's books at an auction.
我在拍賣場上買了一批廉價的二手兒童讀物。

NONE: › the feeling of pleasure and achievement that you experience in your job when you know that your work is worth doing, or the degree to which your work gives you this feeling
工作滿足感

example: Many people are more interested in job satisfaction than in earning large amounts of money.
與賺大錢相比，許多人更重視工作給予他們的滿足感。

NONE: › If you have job security, your job is likely to be permanent.
職業穩定性
› to divide the duties and the pay of one job between two people who work at different times during the day or week
（兩人）分擔一份工作
› someone who does not work regularly for one person or organization but does small pieces of work for different people
臨時演員／打零工的建築工人／打零工的園丁（等等）
› unemployed
失業的
› unemployed people
失業者，失業人士

example: He's been jobless for the past six months.
他已失業六個月了。
The council has been running training schemes for the jobless.
政務委員會一直在實施針對失業者的培訓計劃。
The jobless total (= the number of people unemployed) reached four million this week.
失業人數本周達到400萬。

NONE: › work that someone in an important position gives to their friends or relations
（身居要職的人）為親朋好友安排的工作
› someone who is trying to find a job
求職者
› in the UK, money that the government pays to unemployed people who are looking for a job
（英國）失業補貼
› someone who always obeys all the rules of their job even when they cause problems for other people or when the rules are silly
墨守成規者（即使在為他人帶來麻煩或者制度本身很愚蠢的情況下，依然照章辦事的人）
